title: Grateful Dead Live at Veterans' Memorial Coliseum on 1982-09-23

ai_review.summary: Audience‑recorded tape captures a high‑energy early‑80s Dead show with smoking renditions of The Other One, Throwing Stones and Baby Blue.
ai_review.review: The recording is a solid audience capture that sounds consistently clear for a crowd source, letting the night’s excitement shine through.  Highlights include a blistering The Other One/Too transition, a soaring Throwing Stones debut, and a heartfelt Baby Blue finale, while the first set starts a bit loose but quickly finds its groove.  Overall the performance feels vibrant and memorable despite the inevitable limits of an audience tape.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show 4‑5 stars, praising both musical energy and decent sound quality; the weighted average of show (≈4.3) and recording (≈4.0) yields a strong 4.2 rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Consistently clear for an audience tape; some reviewers note it never fully does the night justice, but overall sound is steady with no major drop‑outs.

poor_songs: Alabama (first‑set opener noted as a bit sloppy)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set starts rough but tightens quickly; second set is strong, especially after the post‑drum segment and features powerful transitions.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple mentions of his high‑voltage guitar work, a soaring Sailor solo, and rhythmic playing during drum jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Praised for vocal power and slide guitar on The Other One (Rooster) plus strong delivery on Greatest Story Ever Told and Althea.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s vocal contribution noted on Johnny B. Goode; overall keyboards support the high energy of the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: The post‑drum “rhythm devils” segment is highlighted as a major lift; drummers (Bill/Mickey) receive strong praise for feeding the jam.
